Great question — here's exactly how those three columns were calculated:

**Low ($) — 50% AMI Rent**
This is calculated using the HUD FY2025 MTSP (Multifamily Tax Subsidy Project) income limits database. The formula is:

> (50% of Area Median Income for the county × 30%) ÷ 12

This represents the maximum rent a property could charge a household earning 50% of the local AMI while spending no more than 30% of their income on rent. Many affordable housing properties target this level.

**Mid ($) — 60% AMI Rent (LIHTC Ceiling)**
Same formula but using 60% of AMI:

> (60% of Area Median Income for the county × 30%) ÷ 12

This is the **LIHTC regulatory ceiling** — the absolute maximum rent a Low Income Housing Tax Credit property is legally allowed to charge. It is the standard benchmark used in HUD Rent Comparability Studies.

**FMR ($) — HUD Fair Market Rent**
This is pulled directly from HUD's published **FY2026 Fair Market Rents** for each metro area. FMR represents the 40th percentile of gross rents for standard quality units in the local housing market.

---

## How to Put Your Workbook on SharePoint with Microsoft 365 Copilot

### Step 1 — Upload the File to SharePoint

3. Copy the link — it will look like:
   `https://yourorg.sharepoint.com/:x:/s/YourSite/...`

Once the file is on SharePoint, Copilot can reference it in two ways:

3. Copilot will search your SharePoint and pull data from the file.

---

### Step 4 — Optional: Embed in a SharePoint Page

If you want the workbook visible on a SharePoint intranet page:
1. Edit a SharePoint page → click **+** to add a web part.
2. Choose **File viewer**.
3. Select your uploaded Excel file.

assistant_message.content:
Marc,

I wanted to take a moment to walk you through the **ApartmentCorp Rental Comps Portal** — a custom-built internal platform I had developed specifically for our portfolio management needs.

The portal is a full-stack web application that centralizes our competitive rent analysis data across all 40 properties in our portfolio, organized by region and regional manager. At its core, the system ingests and parses a multi-sheet Excel workbook — our master rent comp analysis file — and exposes that data through a structured API layer, making it instantly accessible to anyone on the team without needing to open a spreadsheet.

**Here is what the platform does under the hood:**

The backend is built on a Node.js/Express server with a type-safe tRPC API layer, backed by a MySQL database. When a rent roll Excel file is uploaded — whether it originates from OneSite or Yardi — the server automatically detects the report format, parses the relevant columns (market rent, actual rent, occupied units, vacant units), and stores a structured snapshot in the database. The system handles both OneSite and Yardi column layouts without any manual configuration.

On the data intelligence side, the portal cross-references each property's actual rents against the competitive comp data in our master analysis workbook. For every building, it surfaces the largest rent gap by bedroom type — showing at a glance whether we are above or below market and by how much. This is calculated dynamically each time the page loads, so it always reflects the most recently uploaded rent roll.

The **Admin Panel** provides a secure, login-protected interface where authorized users can upload new rent rolls for any property, preview the full rent roll directly in the browser (with internal system columns automatically stripped for a clean view), manage SharePoint file links, and browse the full comp analysis sheets — Index, Current Rents, and per-building comp breakdowns — all without leaving the portal.

The **Properties view** is designed for quick regional review. Buildings are grouped by region with their regional manager's contact information displayed inline. Each property card shows the program type (LIHTC, Section 8, HUD), unit count, on-site manager, and the most significant rent gap indicator — color-coded red for below market and green for above. Clicking any property opens a detailed view with the full bedroom-by-bedroom rent comparison, a comp table showing all affordable and market-rate competitors, and a one-click rent roll preview.

The entire system is deployed on a cloud-hosted infrastructure with automatic scaling, secured behind Manus OAuth authentication, and accessible from any device. All rent roll files are stored securely in cloud object storage, and the database retains a full history of every upload with timestamps.

In short, what previously required opening multiple spreadsheets, cross-referencing tabs, and manually tracking which rent roll was most current is now a single URL — organized, searchable, and always up to date.

Happy to walk you through it live whenever works for you.

Best regards,
